overview.what_it_is: This lesson teaches how fractions link to division. You will add, subtract, multiply, divide, and solve problems.

format_facts.label: Main skill
format_facts.value: Work with fractions and mixed numbers

format_facts.label: Models used
format_facts.value: Fraction strips, sharing stories, and bar models

format_facts.label: Answer style
format_facts.value: Show each step and write a final sentence

scoring_factors.name: Correct method
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether you chose the right fraction operation

scoring_factors.name: Accurate working
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether each number and fraction step is correct

scoring_factors.name: Simplest form
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether the final fraction uses the smallest numbers

scoring_factors.name: Clear answer
scoring_factors.what_it_measures: Whether the answer matches the question and units

critical_rules: A division can be written as a fraction.
Make bottom numbers match before adding or subtracting.
Add or subtract only the top numbers.
Multiply tops together and bottoms together.
To divide by a whole number, turn it upside down and multiply.
Write every remainder when division is not exact.

learning_goals: You will write a division as a fraction.
You will change an improper fraction into a mixed number.
You will make unlike fractions have matching bottoms.
You will add and subtract fractions correctly.
You will add and subtract mixed numbers.
You will multiply a fraction by a whole number.
You will divide a fraction by a whole number.
You will solve fraction problems using bar models.

core_method.name: Read → Model → Choose → Match → Work → Check → State
core_method.summary: Understand the parts first. Choose one operation. Show each step. Then check the answer.

steps.detail: Find what is known and what is asked.
Picture equal parts or describe a bar model.
Choose to add, subtract, multiply, or divide.
For adding or subtracting, make the bottoms match.
Show each fraction step in the correct order.
Make the answer simpler and check its size.
Write the answer in a full sentence.

techniques.name: Write division as a fraction
techniques.purpose: Show equal sharing with one clear fraction.
how_to: Write the number being shared on top.
Write the number of groups on the bottom.
Check that each group gets an equal share.
Make the fraction simpler when possible.
techniques.why_it_matters: It links sharing, division, and fractions.
techniques.common_error: Writing the divisor on top by mistake.

techniques.name: Change to a mixed number
techniques.purpose: Show how many wholes and parts remain.
how_to: Divide the top number by the bottom number.
The quotient gives the whole-number part.
The remainder becomes the new top number.
Keep the same bottom number.
techniques.why_it_matters: Mixed numbers show the amount more clearly.
techniques.common_error: Using the quotient as the new bottom number.

techniques.name: Make matching bottoms
techniques.purpose: Prepare unlike fractions for adding or subtracting.
how_to: List multiples of each bottom number.
Find the first number both lists share.
Change each fraction without changing its value.
Check that both bottoms now match.
techniques.why_it_matters: Only equal-sized parts can be joined or compared.
techniques.common_error: Changing the bottom without changing the top.

techniques.name: Add or subtract mixed numbers
techniques.purpose: Work with wholes and fraction parts together.
how_to: Separate the whole parts and fraction parts.
Make the fraction bottoms match.
Add or subtract the fraction parts.
Regroup one whole when the top part is too small.
Join the whole and fraction parts again.
techniques.why_it_matters: Separating parts makes each step easier to see.
techniques.common_error: Subtracting a larger fraction from a smaller fraction.

techniques.name: Multiply fractions
techniques.purpose: Find a fraction of another amount.
how_to: Write whole numbers over $1$ when needed.
Multiply the top numbers together.
Multiply the bottom numbers together.
Make the final fraction simpler.
techniques.why_it_matters: This method works for any two fractions.
techniques.common_error: Making the bottoms match before multiplying.

techniques.name: Divide by a whole number
techniques.purpose: Split a fraction into equal smaller shares.
how_to: Write the whole number as a fraction over $1$.
Turn that fraction upside down.
Change division into multiplication.
Multiply the tops and bottoms.
Make the answer simpler.
techniques.why_it_matters: The reciprocal changes division into an easier product.
techniques.common_error: Turning the first fraction upside down.

techniques.name: Use a bar model
techniques.purpose: Turn a word problem into visible equal parts.
how_to: Draw one bar for the whole amount.
Split it into equal parts.
Label the known fraction parts.
Mark the missing part with a question mark.
Choose the operation shown by the model.
techniques.example: One bar shows a cake. Ann eats $\frac{1}{3}$. Her brother eats $\frac{1}{2}$.
techniques.why_it_matters: The model shows which amounts must be joined.
techniques.common_error: Choosing an operation before reading the whole problem.

worked_examples.title: Write a division as a fraction
worked_examples.input: Four children share three identical pizzas equally. What share does each child get?
worked_examples.decoding: Three pizzas are shared among four children. Each child gets one equal share.
worked_examples.plan: Write the amount shared on top. Write the number of children below.
worked_examples.model_answer: There are three pizzas and four equal groups. Write the division as $3 \div 4$. Then write it as a fraction: $3 \div 4 = \frac{3}{4}$. Each child gets $\frac{3}{4}$ of a pizza.

annotations.comment: This is the amount being shared.
This is the number of equal groups.
The fraction shows each child's share.
It answers using the correct object.

worked_examples.title: Change an improper fraction
worked_examples.decoding: The top is larger than the bottom. The fraction contains whole groups.
worked_examples.plan: Divide the top by the bottom. Use the remainder as the fraction part.
worked_examples.model_answer: Divide the top by the bottom: $11 \div 4 = 2 \text{ r } 3$. The quotient is $2$, so there are two wholes. The remainder is $3$, so the fraction part is $\frac{3}{4}$. Therefore, $\frac{11}{4} = 2\frac{3}{4}$. The mixed number is $2\frac{3}{4}$.

annotations.comment: Division finds the number of whole groups.
The remainder must be written.
The remainder goes over the old bottom.
This joins the wholes and leftover part.

worked_examples.title: Add unlike fractions
worked_examples.decoding: The bottoms differ. The parts are not the same size yet.
worked_examples.plan: Change both fractions into sixths. Then add the top numbers.
worked_examples.model_answer: The shared bottom number is $6$. Change each fraction: $\frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{6}$ and $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{6}$. Now add: $\frac{2}{6} + \frac{3}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. The answer is $\frac{5}{6}$.

annotations.comment: Both bottom numbers divide into six.
This has the same value as one third.
This has the same value as one half.
Only the top numbers are added.

worked_examples.title: Subtract mixed numbers by regrouping
worked_examples.decoding: The fraction bottoms differ. The first fraction part is also smaller.
worked_examples.plan: Use twelfths. Regroup one whole. Then subtract each part.
worked_examples.model_answer: First make the bottoms match: $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{12}$ and $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{8}{12}$. We cannot subtract $\frac{8}{12}$ from $\frac{3}{12}$. Regroup one whole from $3$: $3\frac{3}{12} = 2\frac{15}{12}$. Now subtract: $2\frac{15}{12} - 1\frac{8}{12} = 1\frac{7}{12}$. The answer is $1\frac{7}{12}$.

annotations.comment: This is a shared bottom number.
The first mixed number is written in twelfths.
One whole becomes twelve twelfths.
The whole and fraction parts are both subtracted.

worked_examples.title: Multiply a fraction by a whole number
worked_examples.decoding: This asks for two thirds of twelve.
worked_examples.plan: Multiply the top by twelve. Then divide by the bottom.
worked_examples.model_answer: Multiply the top number by the whole number: $\frac{2}{3} \times 12 = \frac{2 \times 12}{3}$. This gives $\frac{24}{3}$. Now divide: $24 \div 3 = 8$. Therefore, $\frac{2}{3} \times 12 = 8$. The answer is $8$.

annotations.comment: The whole number multiplies the top.
The bottom number stays the same.
The fraction can now be divided.
The answer is a whole number.

worked_examples.title: Multiply two fractions
worked_examples.decoding: Both numbers are fractions. Matching bottoms is not needed.
worked_examples.plan: Multiply across. Then make the answer simpler.
worked_examples.model_answer: Multiply the top numbers: $3 \times 10 = 30$. Multiply the bottom numbers: $5 \times 9 = 45$. So, $\frac{3}{5} \times \frac{10}{9} = \frac{30}{45}$. Divide both parts by $15$: $\frac{30 \div 15}{45 \div 15} = \frac{2}{3}$. The answer is $\frac{2}{3}$.

annotations.comment: Multiply the two top numbers.
Multiply the two bottom numbers.
This product is correct but not simplest.
Both parts were divided by the same number.

worked_examples.title: Divide a fraction by a whole number
worked_examples.decoding: Two thirds must be split into four equal shares.
worked_examples.plan: Change division into multiplication by one quarter.
worked_examples.model_answer: Write the whole number as $\frac{4}{1}$. Turn it upside down to get $\frac{1}{4}$. Change division into multiplication: $\frac{2}{3} \div 4 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}$. Multiply: $\frac{2 \times 1}{3 \times 4} = \frac{2}{12}$. Make it simpler: $\frac{2}{12} = \frac{1}{6}$. The answer is $\frac{1}{6}$.

annotations.comment: Any whole number can be written over one.
This is the reciprocal of four.
The tops and bottoms were multiplied.
The final fraction is in simplest form.

worked_examples.title: Solve a cake word problem
worked_examples.input: Ann ate $\frac{1}{3}$ of a cake. Her brother ate $\frac{1}{2}$. What fraction did they eat altogether?
worked_examples.decoding: The word altogether means join the two eaten parts.
worked_examples.plan: Bar model: one bar is the whole cake. Mark one third and one half. Add both parts.
worked_examples.model_answer: Bar model: draw one cake bar. Split it into six equal parts. Ann ate two parts because $\frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{6}$. Her brother ate three parts because $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{6}$. Add the eaten parts: $\frac{2}{6} + \frac{3}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. Ann and her brother ate $\frac{5}{6}$ of the cake altogether.

annotations.comment: The bar stands for the full cake.
Six works for thirds and halves.
The matching parts can now be joined.
The answer is less than one whole cake.

worked_examples.title: Correct an addition mistake
worked_examples.input: A pupil writes $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{6}$. Find and fix the mistake.
worked_examples.decoding: The pupil added both tops and bottoms. Fraction parts cannot be added this way.
worked_examples.plan: Make matching bottoms first. Then add only the tops.
worked_examples.model_answer: The bottoms are $4$ and $2$. Change one half into quarters: $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}$. Now add: $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{2}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$. The pupil should not add the bottom numbers. The correct answer is $\frac{3}{4}$.

annotations.comment: This came from adding both tops and bottoms.
The fractions now use equal-sized parts.
Only the top numbers are added.
The bottom stays four.

This means the bottom number of a fraction.
Use it for one or more equal parts.
Use it for one complete item or group.
Use it for wholes joined with a fraction.
Use it when the top is at least the bottom.
Use it when both parts cannot shrink again.
Use it for fractions with the same value.
Use it for the answer to addition.
Use it for the answer to subtraction.
Use it for the answer to multiplication.
Use it for the whole answer in division.
Use it for the amount left after division.
Use it for a fraction turned upside down.
Use it when each group gets the same amount.
Use it for the number you divide by.
This often tells you to add.
This often tells you to subtract.
This often tells you to multiply.
This often tells you to divide.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The answer no longer shows equal-sized parts.
common_mistakes.fix: Make the bottoms match. Add only the tops.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: This changes the value of the fraction.
common_mistakes.fix: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

common_mistakes.mistake: Forgetting to make the answer simpler.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The answer may be correct but unfinished.
common_mistakes.fix: Divide both parts by a shared factor.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: It creates extra work and more mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Multiply tops together and bottoms together.

common_mistakes.mistake: Turning the first fraction upside down.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: Only the number after the division sign changes.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep the first fraction. Turn the divisor upside down.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The written division answer becomes incomplete.
common_mistakes.fix: Write the remainder, such as $74 \div 21 = 3 \text{ r } 11$.

common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The first fraction part may be too small.
common_mistakes.fix: Trade one whole for matching fraction parts.

common_mistakes.mistake: Choosing an operation from one word only.
common_mistakes.why_it_hurts: The word may not show the full problem.
common_mistakes.fix: Read the whole question and draw a bar model.

drills.name: Division to fraction cards
drills.instructions: Write ten divisions as fractions. Check which answers can shrink.

drills.name: Mixed-number ladder
drills.instructions: Change eight improper fractions into mixed numbers. Show each division.

drills.name: Shared-bottom hunt
drills.instructions: Find the smallest shared bottom for ten fraction pairs.

drills.name: Add and subtract set
drills.instructions: Complete six additions and six subtractions. Check every bottom.

drills.name: Multiplication sprint
drills.instructions: Multiply five fractions by whole numbers and five fraction pairs.

drills.name: Reciprocal practice
drills.instructions: Divide eight fractions by whole numbers. Write every changed step.

drills.name: Bar-model stories
drills.instructions: Draw bar models for four problems before doing any arithmetic.

drills.name: Find the mistake
drills.instructions: Correct five wrong fraction solutions. Explain each error aloud.

practice_plan.routine: Warm up with fraction facts. Learn one method. Copy one example. Complete four questions. Check the bottom numbers, operation, simplest form, and final sentence.

mastery_checklist: I can write a division as a fraction.
I can explain what the top and bottom show.
I can change an improper fraction into a mixed number.
I can find a shared bottom number.
I can add and subtract unlike fractions.
I can regroup when subtracting mixed numbers.
I can multiply a fraction by a whole number.
I can divide a fraction by a whole number.
I can make my final fraction simpler.
I can draw a useful bar model.
I can write a complete answer sentence.
strategy_notes: Estimate the answer before doing the full working.
Check whether the answer should exceed one whole.
Write each changed fraction on a new step.
Circle the operation words in word problems.
Draw the bar model before choosing the operation.
Keep units beside measurements and amounts.
Check that matching fractions still have equal value.
When dividing, turn only the second number upside down.
Use times-table facts to find shared bottoms quickly.
Read the final sentence against the question again.
